title: General Knowledge Composed
description: Fifteen two-part questions on world facts, science, geography and culture. Part 1 sets the topic; Part 2 asks the harder follow-up.

questions.question_text: 1. Part 1 — What is the capital of Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: Addis Ababa is Ethiopia’s capital and the seat of the African Union.

questions.question_text: 1. Part 2 — Which continental organisation has its headquarters in Addis Ababa?
questions.explanation: The African Union is headquartered in Addis Ababa.

questions.question_text: 2. Part 1 — Which planet do we live on?
questions.explanation: Earth is our home planet.

questions.question_text: 2. Part 2 — Which planet currently has the most known moons?
questions.explanation: Saturn currently has more confirmed moons than any other planet in the solar system.

questions.question_text: 3. Part 1 — Which ocean is the largest?
questions.explanation: The Pacific is Earth’s largest and deepest ocean.

questions.question_text: 3. Part 2 — Which ocean is the smallest?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean is the smallest of the five oceans.

questions.question_text: 4. Part 1 — Which element has the chemical symbol Au?
questions.explanation: Au comes from the Latin word for gold, aurum.

questions.question_text: 4. Part 2 — Which element has the chemical symbol Fe?
questions.explanation: Fe comes from the Latin word for iron, ferrum.

questions.question_text: 5. Part 1 — Who painted The Starry Night?
questions.explanation: Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in 1889.

questions.question_text: 5. Part 2 — In which country was Vincent van Gogh born?
questions.explanation: Van Gogh was born in the Netherlands in 1853.

questions.question_text: 6. Part 1 — Which invention is associated with Johannes Gutenberg?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg developed movable-type printing in Europe.

questions.question_text: 6. Part 2 — Who is widely credited with patenting the telephone?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell was awarded a US patent for the telephone in 1876.

questions.question_text: 7. Part 1 — Which country is home to Machu Picchu?
questions.explanation: The Inca citadel of Machu Picchu stands in Peru.

questions.question_text: 7. Part 2 — In which mountain range does Machu Picchu stand?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu sits high in the Andes.

questions.question_text: 8. Part 1 — What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
questions.explanation: Diamond ranks highest on the Mohs hardness scale.

questions.question_text: 8. Part 2 — Which gas do plants absorb during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and light to make sugars.

questions.question_text: 9. Part 1 — Which language has the most native speakers worldwide?
questions.explanation: Mandarin Chinese has the largest native-speaker population.

questions.question_text: 9. Part 2 — Which language is most widely spoken worldwide when second-language speakers are included?
questions.explanation: English is the most widely used language when second-language speakers are counted.

questions.question_text: 10. Part 1 — In which year did World War II end?
questions.explanation: World War II ended in 1945.

questions.question_text: 10. Part 2 — Which two Japanese cities were struck by atomic bombs in 1945?
questions.explanation: The United States dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945.

questions.question_text: 11. Part 1 — Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969.

questions.question_text: 11. Part 2 — In which year did the first Moon landing take place?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon in 1969.

questions.question_text: 12. Part 1 — How many continents are commonly counted on Earth?
questions.explanation: The usual school list is seven continents.

questions.question_text: 12. Part 2 — Which continent is the largest by land area?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent by land area.

questions.question_text: 13. Part 1 — What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.explanation: A water molecule is two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.question_text: 13. Part 2 — At what temperature on the Celsius scale does water freeze at standard pressure?
questions.explanation: Water freezes at 0°C at standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.question_text: 14. Part 1 — Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
questions.explanation: William Shakespeare wrote Romeo and Juliet.

questions.question_text: 14. Part 2 — In which Italian city is Romeo and Juliet set?
questions.explanation: The play is set in Verona.

questions.question_text: 15. Part 1 — In which city would you find the Eiffel Tower?
questions.explanation: The Eiffel Tower stands in Paris.

questions.question_text: 15. Part 2 — In which country are the Great Pyramids of Giza?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramids stand at Giza in Egypt.
